subject: Emotions
title: Memory and Sadness
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Memory and Sadness.

hook.text: Sad people remember negative events more accurately. Happiness makes memory rosier and less precise.

buildup.text: This is 'mood-congruent memory.' Your emotional state acts as a filter on what you recall.

discovery.text: Gordon Bower showed that people learn material better when tested in the same mood they studied in.

twist.text: This creates a trap. Sadness recalls sad memories, which deepen the sadness, which recalls worse memories.

climax.text: Breaking the cycle requires external input—a friend, a walk, a change of scene interrupts the loop.

punchline.text: Sadness doesn't just color the present. It rewrites the past.
